palette.notes: Code: 11 colours, one ramp, no hue shift: the NES castle set (black, greys, lava red-orange, Mario red/skin/brown, Bowser green). The close-up cutaway reuses the same flat reds and skin, no shading ramps.

lighting: None: flat NES colours on black; the close-up is flat fills with one darker skin tone for the cheek/nose.
silhouette: Tiny 16 px Mario vs. bigger Bowser on the bridge; in the cutaway Mario's head is blown up to fill the frame with a chunky low-res outline.

motion.timing: Code: median hold 33.3 ms, 29.61 changes/s (moving hammers and flames); Mario himself stands still in a held pose while hammers rain down.

texture: Hard NES pixels, no dither (0.0008); the cutaway uses a much bigger pixel size, mixing pixel scales on purpose.
camera: Locked NES scroll view; two hard cuts to a huge low-res close-up of Mario (a meme reaction shot) and back.

acting.enters: Mario runs in through the castle, dodging fireballs.
acting.acts: Bowser jumps and throws a storm of hammers; Mario just stands; cut to big Mario face doing a smug/unbothered pose, cut back and he takes Bowser out.
acting.depth: Same plane game view; depth faked by cutting to a giant close-up of the tiny sprite.

techniques: meme cutaway: tiny game sprite cut to a giant chunky close-up
character ignores the danger (held pose) for comedy
mixed pixel scales: native sprite vs. 8x blown-up portrait
recognisable game UI kept as a context frame
feel: stock NES 11-colour scene + hero frozen under a hammer storm + giant close-up cutaway = deadpan meme punch
for_fred: When chaos hits, keep Fred still (held pose) and cut once to a big chunky close-up of his face for the reaction, then cut back; one cutaway beats more animation.
